opportunities.title: Authors' Contingency Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all professional authors resident in the UK or British citizens (fiction writers, illustrators, literary translators, scriptwriters, poets, journalists and others) for whom author-related activities make up a substantial amount of annual income. Not open to editors, copywriters, or salaried journalists. Applicants should have been actively engaged in writing over the past 3 years with writing as primary income source. Membership of the SoA not required. Recipients must wait four full calendar years before reapplying.
opportunities.summary: Small, short-term hardship grants to established professional authors in financial difficulty, to help them return to normal working practice. Can cover lost income, shortfalls from projects falling through, impact of illness, sudden homelife changes, and one-off expenses (e.g. boiler, laptop).

opportunities.title: Authors' Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to writers previously published or with a contract for their project with a commercial UK or Irish publisher. For book projects: commissioned by a commercial UK/Irish publisher, or have had at least one book commercially published by a UK/Irish publisher with strong likelihood of next book being published in UK/Ireland. For scripts: previously had a work professionally performed or under contract. Must have non-contributory contract. Hybrid/self-published, editors, AI-generated works not eligible. Recipients must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help develop a work-in-progress (fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects). No deadlines; accepts submissions on a rolling basis. Applicants automatically considered for associated named awards (Eric Ambler, Taner Baybars, John Brooks, Antonia Fraser, Arthur Welton, Great Britain Sasakawa Grant).

opportunities.title: K Blundell Trust
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under the age of 40 on Sunday 1 March 2026; British by birth and currently resident in the United Kingdom; have a previous work of which they are the sole author published with a commercial UK publisher. Recipients must wait four years before re-applying. Cannot apply to both K Blundell Trust and Authors' Foundation in the same calendar year.
opportunities.summary: Work-in-progress grants for British authors under the age of 40 whose work aims to increase social awareness. Accepts fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. Currently closed and will re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Society of Authors' Access Fund

amount.raw: small grants (usually £150 or less); applications for over £150 accepted

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all authors (anyone who creates work for publication, broadcast or performance) who meet SoA membership criteria; open to UK and Irish residents and British and Irish citizens. Membership not required. Applicants may only apply for one grant per calendar year.
opportunities.summary: Small grants for travel, subsistence, childcare or access needs for events, residencies and retreats. Currently closed and expected to re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Strachey Trust Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all authors (as defined by SoA criteria for Full Membership, though membership not required) who are UK resident or British citizens, working on a specific full-length literary project with strong likelihood of publication. One application per calendar year; successful applicants must wait four years before re-applying. Applicants generally expected to fund at least 25% of costs themselves.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable authors to travel to a UK or Republic of Ireland archive or collection to research manuscript material for a specific full-length literary project with a strong likelihood of publication. Can cover travel, accommodation, subsistence, childcare/carer support, access needs, copyright permission fees.
